key_insight: Different flow paths can produce the same flow matching objective but very different SGD variance and convergence speed, so path choice is an optimization lever, not just a modeling detail.
engineering_relevance: For practical generative modeling, choosing a lower-variance path can reduce training cost and improve convergence without changing the target distributional problem.
method: Analyze stochastic-gradient variance in flow matching under different paths g_t
Derive optimal paths for linear Gaussian settings and a PathOpt_θ formulation for general cases
Convert uncheckable path constraints into sample-estimable constraints for numerical search
evidence_signal: The paper supports the theory with experiments on Gaussian data, Gaussian mixture models, and real datasets.
watch_item: Variance reduction must respect the constraint g_t \in G(p_t,v^\star_t); otherwise a lower-variance path may actually slow convergence or change the FM problem.
paper_title: Same Flow, Different Paths: Variance Reduction in Flow Matching
